extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent practitioners and patent examiners (applicants, attorneys/agents handling continuations/divisionals/CPAs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on filing, processing, and examination requirements and defects for continuation, divisional, and Continued Prosecution Applications (CPAs) under 37 CFR 1.53(b)/(d) and related rules; intended to govern practitioner and examiner behavior for U.S. prosecution of continuing applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 47 status handling in continuation/divisional
rubrics_metrics.description: Where 'Rule 47' status has been accorded to the continuation or divisional application, the Office will state that 'Rule 47' status has been accorded but will not repeat the notice to the nonsigning inventor nor the announcement in the Official Gazette. See 37 CFR 1.47(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Rule 47 notice language; do not repeat nonsigning-inventor notice or Gazette announcement in the continuation/divisional file. (Brief mention; procedural note.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of power of attorney/correspondence address identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the power of attorney or correspondence address was changed during prosecution of the prior application, the change must be identified in the continuation or divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not identified in the continuation/divisional, the Office may not recognize the change in that continuing application. (Cites 37 CFR 1.63(d)(4).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Small entity status assertion required in continuing application
rubrics_metrics.description: If small entity status was established in a parent application and is still proper and desired in a continuation or divisional filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b), a new assertion as to continued entitlement to small entity status under 37 CFR 1.27 is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must reassert small-entity entitlement in the 1.53(b) application; see MPEP § 509.03 for procedure and form guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits/declarations from prior application not automatically carried forward (1.53(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations (e.g., under 37 CFR 1.130, 1.131, 1.132) filed during prosecution of the prior nonprovisional application do not automatically become part of a continuation or divisional filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicant desires to rely on earlier affidavits/declarations, make remarks of record in the 1.53(b) application and include a copy of the original affidavit/declaration. Use form paragraph 2.03 for instructions. Examiner note: do not use form paragraph 2.03 for 1.53(d) applications because in 1.53(d) such affidavits/declarations automatically become part of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time for continuity must be filed as separate petition in prior application
rubrics_metrics.description: If an extension of time is necessary to establish continuity between the prior application and a continuing application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b), the petition for an extension must be filed as a separate paper directed to the prior nonprovisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 37 CFR 1.136(a)(3), an authorization to charge fees may be treated as a constructive petition in concurrent/future replies, but a continuing application is a new application and not a 'reply' to the prior application's last Office action. Thus the petition and fee (37 CFR 1.17) must be filed in the prior application, accompanied by certificate of mailing (1.8) or Express Mail (1.10) if those benefits are desired. Examples provided to illustrate timing consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior application not automatically abandoned by filing continuing application
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.53(b) and 1.63(d) practice, the prior nonprovisional application is not automatically abandoned upon filing of the continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To expressly abandon the prior application, file a paper signed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.138. A practitioner not of record may expressly abandon the prior application as of the continuing application's filing date when filing the continuing application (see 37 CFR 1.34). If the prior application had an issue fee paid, a petition under 37 CFR 1.313 to withdraw from issue is required before abandonment. If the prior is before the Board, send separate notice to the Board. CAFC mandate terminates proceedings after affirmed rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-action final practice and preliminary amendments in continuations/divisionals
rubrics_metrics.description: First action final practice applies to continuation and divisional applications filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b). Any preliminary amendment present on the filing date of such an application is part of the original disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must comply with 37 CFR 1.121 (e.g., complete claim listing when claims are added/canceled/amended). Classify and assign to the appropriate Technology Center considering the claims as they will appear after entry of such preliminary amendments. See MPEP §§ 706.07(b) and 714.

rubrics_metrics.name: New matter in copied oath/declaration requires new oath and redesignation as CIP
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a copy of the oath or declaration from a prior application was filed in a continuation/divisional and the examiner determines new matter is present relative to the prior application, the examiner should so notify the applicant and require a new oath/declaration with surcharge (37 CFR 1.16(f)) and that the application be redesignated as a continuation-in-part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferably notify applicant in the next Office action (ideally the first Office action). See MPEP § 608.04(b) for procedure when new matter appears in a preliminary amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling missing pages/drawings and incorporation by reference (pre- and post- Sept 21, 2004)
rubrics_metrics.description: If examiner finds pages of the specification or drawings missing and the continuation/divisional filed prior to Sept 21, 2004 used a copy of the oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.63(d), check whether the continuation/divisional as originally filed includes a statement incorporating by reference the prior application(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pre-9/21/2004 apps the incorporation statement could appear in the transmittal letter. If incorporation statement is missing and applicant not informed of omitted items, return the application to OIPE for a 'Notice of Omitted Item(s)'. For apps filed on/after 9/21/2004, follow 37 CFR 1.57(a) and MPEP § 201.17.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA availability limited to design applications (37 CFR 1.53(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation or divisional (but not a continuation-in-part) application may be filed as a Continued Prosecution Application (CPA) under 37 CFR 1.53(d) provided the prior nonprovisional application is a design application that is complete as defined by 37 CFR 1.51(b), and other timing conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPA practice is available only for design applications meeting completeness and timing requirements described in 1.53(d)(1)-(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA practice eliminated for utility and plant applications (effective July 14, 2003)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective July 14, 2003, CPA practice has been eliminated as to utility and plant applications; applicants who wish to continue examination after prosecution is closed should consider filing an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPAs filed prior to July 14, 2003 continue to be processed under prior 1.53(d). Any CPA filed on/after July 14, 2003 in a utility/plant application is improper regardless of the filing date of the underlying application. The Office will not convert an improper CPA into a 1.53(b) application unless extenuating circumstances shown. If an examiner discovers an improper/incomplete CPA processed in error, notify SAE or TC support to reprocess and correct records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper CPA treatment for apps filed on/after June 8, 1995
rubrics_metrics.description: If a utility or plant application has a filing date on/after June 8, 1995, an improper CPA filed on/after July 14, 2003 will be treated as a request for continued examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the improper CPA/RCE lacks required submission or fee under 1.114(e) or prosecution was not closed, Office will treat it as an improper RCE and send Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (PTO-2051). If reply time expired the app is abandoned and reviving requires petition under 1.137 and required fees/submissions. Applicants cannot switch inventions by RCE (37 CFR 1.145); claims to a distinct invention will be withdrawn. Notify applicant using form paragraph 8.26 or 8.27 when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper CPA handling for apps filed before June 8, 1995
rubrics_metrics.description: If a utility/plant application has a filing date before June 8, 1995, the Office cannot treat an improper CPA filed on/after July 14, 2003 as an RCE (RCE practice does not apply to pre-6/8/1995 apps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will notify applicant by Notice of Improper CPA (or FWC) Filing For Utility or Plant Applications Filed Before June 8, 1995, PTO-2011. Time period for reply will continue to run. Applicant may file a continuing application under 37 CFR 1.53(b). If time for reply expired and app is abandoned, revive via petition under 37 CFR 1.137 to establish copendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA advantages and encouraged practice (preliminary amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA has advantages versus filing under 1.53(b): minimal papers required to secure a filing date, Office will not normally issue a new filing receipt, and first Office action delay should be shorter (treated as 'amended' application for examination priority when prior had an OA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are strongly encouraged to file any preliminary amendment in a CPA at the time the CPA is filed (see 37 CFR 1.115 and MPEP § 714.03(a)) because CPAs treated as 'amended' apps generally receive quicker first Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter allowed in CPA; substitute specification rules
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment in a CPA may introduce new matter. Any new specification filed with a CPA request will not be considered part of the original application papers but will be treated as a substitute specification under 37 CFR 1.125; substitute specifications must comply with 1.125(b) (including statement that substitute contains no new matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute specifications containing new matter will be denied entry. Preliminary amendments (other than substitute spec) ordinarily entered; however, any new matter entered will be required to be canceled pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 132 and any claim relying on such new matter will be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph. Applicant may petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to remove substitute spec or preliminary amendment from the CPA file to be treated as a separate application (with filing date equal to CPA filing date), but will not get filing fee refund for a proper CPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA may be based on prior CPA and limits on pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA may be based on a prior CPA so long as the prior CPA is complete under 37 CFR 1.51(b) and is a design application. There is no statutory limit to the number of CPAs in a chain, but only one CPA may be pending at a time based on the same prior nonprovisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may file chains of CPAs for design matters subject to the single-pending-CPA restriction for the same prior application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees, oath/declaration, and original disclosure for CPAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.53(d), the specification, claims, drawings, and any amendments entered in the prior nonprovisional application are used in the CPA. A new basic filing fee, search fee, and examination fee are required (35 U.S.C. 41 and 37 CFR 1.16). The previously filed oath/declaration in the prior application will be considered the oath or declaration of the CPA (CPA cannot contain new matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: no search/exam fees were required for CPAs filed before Dec 8, 2004 (historical exception). Any subject matter added by amendment in the parent app which is new matter in the parent is also new matter in the CPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation as CPA in papers controls treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: If application papers for a design application are designated as a CPA filing under 37 CFR 1.53(d) (e.g., reference to 1.53(d), 'CPA', or 'continued prosecution application'), the papers will be treated as a CPA even if inconsistent designations are present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If utility/plant papers are in any way designated as a CPA, they will be treated as an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114. Applicants seeking alternative treatment must timely file appropriate petitions (e.g., 1.182) before the CPA request is entered into the prior application's file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for filing a CPA (completeness and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation/divisional may be filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) if the prior nonprovisional application is a design application complete as defined by 37 CFR 1.51(b) and the CPA is filed before the earliest of: (A) payment of the issue fee on the prior application (unless petition under 1.313(c) granted), (B) abandonment of the prior application, or (C) termination of proceedings on the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete application per 1.51(b) must include appropriate filing fee(s) and a signed oath/declaration under 1.63. RCE practice under 1.114 is not available in design apps; an improper RCE in a design app will not be treated as a CPA and will not toll reply periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial processing checks for CPA requests (Technology Center verification)
rubrics_metrics.description: The TC will verify that: (A) the prior application is a design application; (B) correct application number identified; (C) request properly signed; (D) prior application was pending and issue fee not paid on or before CPA filing date; (E) prior application was complete under 1.51(b); and (F) proper filing fee paid in the CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If conditions/fees not satisfied, applicant notified and no examination will be made until errors corrected or proper fees submitted (see 37 CFR 1.53(h)). If an examiner discovers improper processing, notify SAE or TC support to reprocess and correct records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorrect application number handling and resubmission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If a CPA request does not properly identify the prior application's number, the TC should attempt to identify the number via other identifying info (inventor name, filing date, title, docket). If identified, enter correct number in red ink and date/initial. If unable to identify and sender is registered practitioner, request practitioner provide letter with correct number; if unsuccessful, return the CPA request to sender (when return address available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If resubmitted with correct number within two weeks of return mail date, original date of receipt will be considered filing date (37 CFR 1.5(a)). Applicants may use Certificate of Mailing (1.8) or Express Mail (1.10) for resubmissions. Two-week period is not extendible; if later resubmitted, the later receipt date is the filing date. Keep copies of returned CPA and date-stamped cover letter in TC record. Image File Wrapper processing guidance referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement for CPA requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA is a request to expressly abandon the prior application and therefore must be properly signed. The individuals who may properly sign are listed in 37 CFR 1.33(b). In joint applications with no attorney/agent, all applicants must sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unsigned or improperly signed CPA will be placed in the file of the prior application and entitled to an application filing date but is ineffective to abandon the prior application. A CPA will NOT be examined until properly signed. A registered practitioner acting in a representative capacity under 1.34 may sign; correspondence will be sent to the correspondence address in the prior application until a new power of attorney or change of address signed by an attorney/agent of record is filed in the CPA. An assignee may sign if accompanied by papers establishing ownership under 37 CFR 3.73(b), unless such papers already filed and ownership unchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date rules and acceptable modes for CPA requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a CPA is the date on which a request on a separate paper for a CPA is filed. A CPA request cannot be submitted as part of papers filed for another purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPA requests may be mailed, faxed, or filed in person. Facsimile filing receipt date is the date complete transmission received by an Office facsimile unit unless completed on a weekend/holiday (then next business day). Applicants may include a 'Receipt for Facsimile Transmitted CPA' (PTO/SB/29A) but it cannot be used as evidence that papers other than the CPA were filed by fax. If filing by fax without authorization to charge fees via PTO-2038, the application will be treated under 1.53(f) as filed without appropriate fees. 37 CFR 1.6(f) prescribes the showing required when Office has no evidence of receipt of a faxed CPA (e.g., sending unit's transmission report).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Mailing/Express Mail inapplicable to CPA filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: The Certificate of Mailing procedure under 37 CFR 1.8 does not apply to filing a request for a CPA, since the filing of such a request is considered filing of national application papers for purposes of obtaining an application filing date (1.8(a)(2)(i)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative example: a certificate of mailing dated within the answer period does not save an otherwise late CPA; timing consequences provided to illustrate that Certificate of Mailing cannot be used to establish CPA filing date for timeliness relative to abandonment and reply periods.
